reason: E2 states that HEA surface heterogeneity provides neighboring sites with different local electronic structures, which can tune selectivity in complex reactions, and cites the IrOsPtPdRhRu 12-electron ethanol oxidation as an example. However, no cited evidence directly supports the claim that thermal annealing reduces this heterogeneity or that such a reduction impairs ethanol oxidation performance; E3 discusses an ordered intermetallic structure with high activity, which could be seen as conflicting with the disorder-activity premise.
premises: Disordered HEA catalysts possess diverse active sites with varied local electronic structures.
This active-site diversity optimizes adsorption and facilitates multi-step electron-proton transfer in ethanol oxidation.
Thermal annealing induces a disorder-to-order transition, reducing active-site heterogeneity.
Reduced heterogeneity impairs the kinetics of the 12-electron oxidation pathway, lowering activity.
